workingTitle: Euclid finds a 360-million-solar-mass black hole at cosmic dawn
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed Astronomy & Astrophysics article and ESA release published November 24, 2026
coreFacts: Euclid identified J1504+6252, nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, in about 18 months of wide-survey data.
Follow-up observations with Keck, the Large Binocular Telescope, Hubble, and JWST confirmed the source as a quasar at redshift 8.13.
The light comes from about 630 million years after the Big Bang, roughly 40 million years earlier than the previous quasar record.
JWST spectroscopy indicates a central black hole mass of approximately 360 million solar masses.
The quasar is currently accreting relatively slowly, implying earlier rapid growth or an unusually massive initial seed.
